rationale.conceptual: The method uses well-established MD potentials (Tersoff, LJ) and simulation procedures (fixed layers, thermostat layers, constant angular velocity) applied to a nanocomposite system. It is a standard method with minor variations, not a novel algorithm.
rationale.execution: The workflow requires 2-3 sequential stages: model construction/equilibration, multiple torsion production runs, and property extraction. All steps use LAMMPS, a single tool, without complex dependencies.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies classical molecular dynamics using standard Tersoff and Lennard-Jones potentials to study torsion of GNR@SWCNT. The method is straightforward but requires non-trivial setup of the atomistic system, torsion application, and stress extraction. The pipeline involves building models, running equilibration and production MD, and analyzing outputs, which is a multi-step but not overly complex workflow. Small system sizes make the resource needs very modest.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Simulations involve <5000 atoms and torsion runs of ~1 ns, which are easily handled by a single CPU core with minimal memory; no external datasets are required.
